chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf, from al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ghiyāth, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام.

The earlobe carries one-third of the blood-money of the ear; the extra finger carries one-third of the blood-money of a finger; and each side of the nose carries one-third of the blood-money of the nose.

key_terms.الْإِصْبَعِ الزَّائِدِ: an extra finger beyond the usual number
key_terms.ثُلُثَ دِيَةِ الْأَنْفِ: one-third of the blood-money of the nose
key_terms.ثُلُثَ دِيَةِ الْإِصْبَعِ: one-third of the blood-money of a finger
key_terms.دِيَةِ الْأُذُنِ: the prescribed blood-money for the ear
key_terms.شَحْمَةِ الْأُذُنِ: the earlobe, treated here as a compensable part of the ear
key_terms.كُلِّ جَانِبٍ مِنَ الْأَنْفِ: each side of the nose considered separately for compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for the earlobe, an extra finger, and each side of the nose in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام regarding specified proportions of diyah for particular body parts. It establishes fractional compensation for injury to the earlobe, an extra finger, and each side of the nose within the framework of Islamic judicial rulings.
